title: Architect Raj Rewal Engages Anant National University Students at Design(ing) Futures Symposium
summary: The eminent architect spoke with students and faculty in Ahmedabad on how India's architectural and cultural traditions can inform contemporary design.
body_html:
Ahmedabad, October 2026: Eminent architect and urban design consultant Ar. Raj Rewal engaged with students and faculty of Anant National University at a symposium held under Design(ing) Futures, an initiative developed with the Global Village Foundation to bring leading voices from architecture and design into conversation with the university's academic community.

Students had the chance to interact directly with the architect, whose work over more than six decades has shaped contemporary Indian architecture. The symposium brought together perspectives from architecture, interiors, art, craft and design, encouraging students to see design as a practice connected to people, culture and society.

A highlight was the screening of Indian Modernity: The Architecture of Raj Rewal, a film on his work and approach. It was followed by a talk by Ar. Rewal and an open interaction in which he discussed how his architecture responds to India's cultural, climatic and social contexts, and how designers work through real-world constraints.

During the symposium, Ar. Rewal also launched the Backpackers Academy of Life Trail 1: Kerala, an initiative of the Global Village Foundation, with its first trail planned across Kerala in December 2026.

The symposium was envisioned by Dr. Sanjeev Vidyarthi, Provost, Anant National University, and curated by Ar. Jabeen Zacharias, Professor of Practice. It was coordinated by Prof. Risha Roy, Associate Professor and Lead, Sustainable Fashion and Textile Design, and Co-lead, Transdisciplinary Design.
